brief.label: UK band and radio rules
brief.text: UHF RFID in the UK operates in the 865-868 MHz lower band — up to 2 W e.r.p. in the 865.6-867.6 MHz high-power channels (200 kHz spacing), 100 mW e.r.p. in 865-865.6 MHz, 500 mW e.r.p. in 867.6-868 MHz — and in the 916.1-918.9 MHz upper band at up to 4 W e.r.p. on centre frequencies 916.3, 917.5 and 918.7 MHz, per Ofcom's UK Interface Requirement 2030. NFC runs at 13.56 MHz worldwide. The UK plan mirrors ETSI EN 302 208, so EU-tuned inlays work unchanged; US-tuned (902-928 MHz) inlays underperform in UK portals. Readers are the regulated radio equipment; passive tags are antenna-tuned, not individually certified.

brief.label: UKCA and CE after Brexit
brief.text: CE marking is recognised in Great Britain indefinitely for 21 product regulations, including the Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/1206), the EMC Regulations 2016 and the RoHS Regulations 2012; the Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/696, in force 1 October 2024) gave the policy statutory effect. UKCA remains available as an alternative conformity route. Northern Ireland follows the EU framework under the Windsor Framework, so CE applies there directly.

brief.label: Data protection
brief.text: Personal data on credentials and in read logs falls under the UK GDPR alongside the Data Protection Act 2018, regulated by the ICO; the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 is amending the framework in phases. The European Commission renewed the UK adequacy decisions on 19 December 2025, so EU-UK personal-data flows continue. Encode the minimum on the card and keep personal records in your access-controlled back end.

brief.label: Landed cost
brief.text: Most RFID cards, tags and labels enter the UK as 'smart cards' under commodity code 8523 52, which carries a 0% duty rate under the UK Global Tariff; import VAT applies at 20%. VAT-registered importers can use postponed VAT accounting to declare and recover import VAT on the same VAT Return. Importing in your own name requires a GB EORI number from HMRC; Proud Tek DDP quotes include duty, VAT and clearance, so the quoted price is the landed price.

brief.label: Lead times to the UK
brief.text: Production runs 5-7 business days after artwork approval; DHL express delivers to any UK address in 4-6 days; most orders arrive 9-13 days door-to-door. Quotations return within one business day, and free samples (typically 3-5 pieces) ship before any production commitment.

sections.title: UKCA and CE: the post-Brexit answer is calmer than the headlines
sections.intro: Three years of 'UKCA deadline' headlines resolved into an anticlimax procurement can enjoy: the CE mark you already require from suppliers still works in Great Britain — indefinitely, and now with statutory force. Here is the 2026 state of play; the full conformity walkthrough (directives, EN standards, technical files) lives in our [CE marking guide for RFID](/guides/rfid-ce-marking-europe/).

sections.title: The UK UHF band: Brexit moved the paperwork, not the physics
sections.intro: Radio physics did not attend the negotiations. Ofcom kept UK RFID on the European band plan, so an inlay tuned for Frankfurt reads just as happily in Felixstowe — the expensive mistake is the pallet of US-tuned 902-928 MHz stock a broker swore was 'global'. Quietly, the UK also opened an upper band with real power headroom. New to frequency planning? Start with the [LF vs HF vs UHF guide](/blog/rfid-frequencies-lf-hf-uhf-explained/).

faq.question: Do you ship to the UK with VAT and duties included?
faq.answer: Yes. We offer DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) shipping to the UK where all import duties, VAT (20%), and customs clearance are included in the quoted price. Goods arrive at your UK address with no additional charges. This simplifies procurement for UK businesses and resellers.

faq.question: Can I resell your NFC cards under my own brand name?
faq.answer: Absolutely. We provide full white-label manufacturing for UK resellers. Your brand name, logo, packaging, and documentation are applied to the product. We do not include any Proud Tek branding on white-label orders. Many successful UK NFC card businesses use us as their manufacturing partner.

faq.question: What NFC chip works best for digital business cards in the UK?
faq.answer: NTAG 213 is the most popular choice. It stores a URL that links to your digital profile (Blinq, HiHello, Popl, or your own website) and is compatible with every iPhone (7 and later) and Android phone with NFC. For profiles requiring more data storage, NTAG 216 offers {chip:nxp-ntag-216:user_bytes} bytes of memory. Both chips work identically on UK smartphones.

faq.question: Do I need UKCA marking to import RFID products from China into Great Britain?
faq.answer: No. CE marking is recognised in Great Britain indefinitely for 21 product regulations, including the Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/1206), and the Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (in force 1 October 2024) gave that policy statutory effect — so CE-marked RFID products can be placed on the GB market without UKCA marking. UKCA remains available as an alternative route, and we supply UKCA-aligned documentation on request. Northern Ireland follows the EU framework under the Windsor Framework, so CE applies there directly.

faq.question: Will EU-band (865-868 MHz) UHF tags work in the UK?
faq.answer: Yes. Ofcom's UK Interface Requirement 2030 keeps UK RFID on the European plan: the 865-868 MHz lower band allows up to 2 W e.r.p. in the 865.6-867.6 MHz high-power channels, matching ETSI EN 302 208, and the UK additionally authorises a 916.1-918.9 MHz upper band at up to 4 W e.r.p. on centre frequencies 916.3, 917.5 and 918.7 MHz. EU-tuned inlays therefore work unchanged in the UK. The combination to avoid is inventory tuned for the US 902-928 MHz band, which sits above the UK lower band and underperforms in UK portals.

faq.question: Do I need an EORI number to buy RFID products from China?
faq.answer: If you act as the importer — under EXW or FOB terms — yes: imports into Great Britain require a GB EORI number, which HMRC issues to GB-established businesses, and your customs declarations and postponed-VAT statements are recorded against it. Under DDP shipping we handle customs clearance as part of delivery, so first-time buyers can order without one. An EORI is free and quick to obtain, so most regular importers get one anyway to keep the option of switching terms.

faq.question: What import duty and VAT apply to RFID cards and tags in the UK?
faq.answer: Most RFID cards, tags and labels classify as 'smart cards' under commodity code 8523520000, which carries a 0% duty rate under the UK Global Tariff. Import VAT applies at the standard 20% rate; VAT-registered UK importers can use postponed VAT accounting to declare and recover import VAT on the same VAT Return instead of paying at the border. Our DDP quotes include duty, VAT and clearance, so the quoted price is the landed price. RFID readers and electronics accessories classify under different commodity codes — check each invoice line.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for UK buyers?
faq.answer: MOQs for UK orders match our standard factory minimums: custom-printed PVC cards start at 500 pieces (digital printing accepts runs as low as 100), NFC inlays and labels at 1,000 pieces (one roll), and silicone wristbands at 500 pieces. NFC business card programmes for resellers typically run in monthly batches of 500+ cards.
